title: Why Middle-Aged Americans Are in Crisis
titleZh: 上有老下有小，中年群体正在被掏空
summary:
在代际研究领域，针对儿童和青少年的研究已相当丰富，对老年群体的关注也同样充分，但中年群体呢？在相关研究中，他们有时就像那个被遗忘的中间孩子。不过，最新发表于《心理科学最新动向》的一项研究，对美国中年群体进行了全面考察，其呈现出的图景并不乐观。

来源：Nautilus；作者：Jake Currie；原文发布时间：2026-04-17 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: There’s plenty of research on children and young adults, and plenty of research on senior citizens, but what about middle-aged people? It can sometimes feel like they’re the forgotten middle child of generational studies. But now, a new paper published in Current Directions in Psychological Science is taking a comprehensive look at middle-aged Americans, and it paints a pretty bleak picture.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在代际研究领域，针对儿童和青少年的研究已相当丰富，对老年群体的关注也同样充分，但中年群体呢？在相关研究中，他们有时就像那个被遗忘的中间孩子。不过，最新发表于《心理科学最新动向》的一项研究，对美国中年群体进行了全面考察，其呈现出的图景并不乐观。

paragraphs.contentEn: Arizona University psychologist Frank Infurna and his team compared survey responses from people between the ages of 40 and 65 today to middle-aged people from 30 years ago. The differences were striking. Compared to earlier generations, loneliness, depression, and memory problems are on the rise. A look at middle-aged people from other economically developed countries revealed no similar declines, and in fact some improvements. In other words, it’s a uniquely American phenomenon.
paragraphs.contentZh: 亚利桑那大学心理学家弗兰克·因富纳及其团队，将当下40至65岁人群的问卷调查数据，与30年前同龄群体的调查结果进行了对比，发现差异十分显著。与上一代中年人相比，如今中年人的孤独感、抑郁水平以及记忆问题均呈上升趋势。相比之下，对其他发达经济体中年群体的考察并未发现类似下滑，部分指标反而有所改善。换句话说，这是美国独有的现象。

paragraphs.contentEn: As for why we’re so down-and-out, according to Infurna, upstream factors like public policy, intermediary factors like career stressors, and downstream, individual-level factors like interpersonal relationships all play a role. For example, “sandwich generation” dynamics are partially to blame for the mid-life declines. Middle-aged people tend to have aging parents who are living longer and requiring more care. At the same time, their adult children may be struggling to navigate difficult job and housing markets to gain their independence. Put simply, being pulled in two directions while juggling individual needs is taking its toll.
paragraphs.contentZh: 至于美国中年人整体状况为何呈现低迷趋势，因富纳指出，从上游的公共政策，到中游的职业压力，再到下游个体层面的人际关系等因素，均在其中发挥作用。例如，“夹心一代”的家庭代际结构，在一定程度上加剧着这一群体的困境。如今的中年人往往需要照料寿命延长、护理需求增加的年迈父母。同时，他们的成年子女也可能在严峻的就业和住房市场中挣扎，难以实现经济独立。简而言之，来自上下两代的拉扯与自身需求的挤压，正不断透支中年一代的身心资源。

paragraphs.contentEn: “It’s a sandwich generation, but on steroids,” Infruna said in a statement. To complicate matters, middle-aged Americans are feeling the same economic crunch as younger generations. Rising costs compounded by labor market instability and less accumulated wealth compared to previous generations have made middle-aged Americans particularly vulnerable to economic swings and career stress. Additionally, middle-aged people in nations with more economic inequality—like the United States—report higher levels of loneliness.
paragraphs.contentZh: 因富纳在一份声明中表示：“这是承受着极限压力的夹心一代。”更严峻的是，美国中年人正承受着与年轻一代同样的经济压力。生活成本攀升、劳动力市场不稳定，以及相较于前几代人更少的财富积累，多重因素叠加，使这一群体在面对经济波动和职业压力时格外脆弱。研究还发现，在经济不平等程度更高的国家（如美国），中年人报告的孤独感水平也更高。

paragraphs.contentEn: “The cost of living is just much higher within the United States, and there are fewer safety nets here,” Infurna said. “If something catastrophic or terrible were to happen health-wise or you lose your job, there’s not a safety net to fall back on compared to in other nations.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 因富纳表示：“美国的生活成本要高得多，同时社会保障也相对有限。与其他国家相比，一旦在健康方面遭遇灾难性或严重的变故，或者失去工作，美国人往往缺乏可以依仗的安全保障。”

paragraphs.contentEn: A more robust safety net, like those in European countries, could help buffer middle-aged adults from economic stress and the cascading negative health effects that follow. Right now, the United States has no federal parental leave policy, no subsidized childcare, and only modest family spending policies compared to European nations. Adopting better support systems for families could go a long way toward breaking middle-aged Americans out of their collective funk. Until then middle-aged Americans will just have to comfort themselves with the knowledge that they had better movies, music, and fashion than other generations.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如果能建立起类似欧洲国家那样更完善的社会保障体系，将有助于缓解中年群体面临的经济压力，减少由此引发的负面健康连锁反应。目前，美国既没有联邦层面的带薪育儿假，也缺乏托育补贴；与欧洲国家相比，其家庭支出政策也相对有限。推行更完善的家庭支持体系，将显著有助于改善美国中年群体的集体心理困境。不过，在这一天到来之前，美国中年人或许只能聊以慰藉：与其他世代相比，他们至少拥有过更出色的电影、音乐和时尚。
